source.text: וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לְדָוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֤ה פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ נִלְחָמִ֣ים בִּקְעִילָ֔ה וְהֵ֖מָּה שֹׁסִ֥ים אֶת־הַגֳּרָנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And told to David, saying, Look, Philistines [are] fighting against Keilah, and they [are] plundering the threshing floors.

en.L: And they told David, saying, "Look, [the] Philistines [are] fighting against Keilah, and they [are] plundering the threshing floors."
en.B: David was told, "The Philistines are attacking Keilah and looting the threshing floors."
en.R: Someone brought David this news: "The Philistines are attacking the town of Keilah. They are stealing the grain from the threshing floors."

fr.L: Et on le rapporta à David, en disant : « Voici, les Philistins combattent contre Qeïla, et ils pillent les aires. »
fr.B: On vint dire à David : « Les Philistins attaquent Qeïla et pillent les aires de battage. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un est venu annoncer à David : « Les Philistins attaquent la ville de Qeïla. Ils volent le grain sur les aires de battage. »

decisions.choice: Keilah: a walled town in the lowland of Judah, near the Philistine border
decisions.reason: Keilah is listed among the towns of the western foothills of Judah (Joshua 15:33, 44). It lay a few hours' walk from Philistine territory, and it had gates and bars (verse 7).

decisions.choice: the threshing floors: where the harvested grain lay
decisions.reason: At harvest the grain was brought to open, hard-packed floors to be threshed and winnowed. Raiders who took it there carried off the town's food for the year, as Midian had done to Israel (Judges 6:3-4, 11).

decisions.choice: they told David: someone brought word; the speakers are not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject and works like a passive: "David was told". David was then in the forest of Hereth in Judah (22:5).

decisions.choice: stealing the grain from the threshing floors
decisions.reason: Readable says what was taken from the threshing floors, and adds "the town of" before the name.

decisions.choice: Qeïla
decisions.reason: A name not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription of the Hebrew, kept the same through both books.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֵלֵ֣ךְ וְהִכֵּ֔יתִי בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּהסוַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד לֵ֚ךְ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֖ אֶת־קְעִילָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired David of Yahweh, saying, Shall I go and strike these the Philistines? And said Yahweh to David, Go, and strike the Philistines and save Keilah.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to David, "Go, and strike the Philistines and save Keilah."
en.B: So David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Am I to go and attack these Philistines?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered David, "Go, attack the Philistines, and rescue Keilah."
en.R: David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I go and fight these Philistines?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told him, "Go. Fight the Philistines and save Keilah."

fr.L: Et David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « Irai-je, et frapperai-je ces Philistins ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à David : « Va, et frappe les Philistins, et sauve Qeïla. »
fr.B: David consulta donc {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « Dois-je aller attaquer ces Philistins ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit à David : « Va, attaque les Philistins et délivre Qeïla. »
fr.R: David a demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Est-ce que je dois aller combattre ces Philistins ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a répondu : « Va. Combats les Philistins et sauve Qeïla. »

decisions.choice: inquired of the LORD: asked God for an answer, probably through a priest or prophet
decisions.reason: Israel sought the LORD's will through the priest with the ephod, or through a prophet (10:22; 14:36-37; 28:6). The prophet Gad was with David (22:5), and verse 6 explains that Abiathar the priest came to him with an ephod. The text does not say which way David asked here.

decisions.choice: save Keilah: rescue it, the work of Israel's deliverers
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the LORD saving Israel through the judges and through Saul himself (Judges 2:16; 1 Samuel 9:16; 11:3). Saul is the king, yet it is David, hunted by Saul, who is sent to rescue a town of Judah.

decisions.choice: asked
decisions.reason: Readable says "asked" for "inquired of", as at 10:22.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י דָוִד֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ פֹ֛ה בִּֽיהוּדָ֖ה יְרֵאִ֑ים וְאַף֙ כִּֽי־נֵלֵ֣ךְ קְעִלָ֔ה אֶל־מַֽעַרְכ֖וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] men of David to him, Look, we here in Judah [are] afraid, and how much more if we go [to] Keilah against [the] battle lines of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And David's men said to him, "Look, we [are] afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go [to] Keilah against the battle lines of [the] Philistines!"
en.B: But David's men said to him, "Even here in Judah we live in fear. How much worse if we go to Keilah to face the Philistine army!"
en.R: But David's men said to him, "We are afraid even here in Judah. It will be much worse if we go to Keilah and fight the Philistine army!"

fr.L: Et les hommes de David lui dirent : « Voici, nous avons peur ici en Juda ; combien plus si nous allons à Qeïla contre les rangs des Philistins ! »
fr.B: Mais les hommes de David lui dirent : « Ici même, en Juda, nous vivons dans la peur. Que sera-ce si nous allons à Qeïla affronter l’armée des Philistins ! »
fr.R: Mais les hommes de David lui ont dit : « Nous avons peur même ici, en Juda. Ce sera bien pire si nous allons à Qeïla pour combattre l’armée des Philistins ! »

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: The two words make the second case stronger than the first: if they are afraid where they are, they will be far more afraid facing an army in battle.

decisions.choice: here in Judah: where they were hiding from Saul
decisions.reason: Keilah also belonged to Judah, so the contrast is not between two territories. In the hills of Judah the men were already in danger from Saul; at Keilah they would have the Philistines in front of them as well.

decisions.choice: battle lines: an army drawn up for battle
decisions.reason: The word means ranks set in order for fighting, as when the Philistines and Israel faced each other in the Valley of Elah (17:8, 10).

decisions.choice: the Philistine army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the army that stands in battle lines rather than the lines themselves.

source.text: וַיּ֨וֹסֶף ע֤וֹד דָּוִד֙ לִשְׁאֹ֣ל בַּֽיהוָ֔הסוַֽיַּעֲנֵ֖הוּ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר ק֚וּם רֵ֣ד קְעִילָ֔ה כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And added again David to inquire of Yahweh, and answered him Yahweh and said, Arise, go down [to] Keilah, for I [am] giving Philistines into your hand.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} yet again, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him and said, "Arise, go down [to] Keilah, for I am giving [the] Philistines into your hand."
en.B: David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} once more, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Set out and go down to Keilah, for I am handing the Philistines over to you."
en.R: So David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go down to Keilah now. I am going to give you victory over the Philistines."

fr.L: Et David consulta encore une fois {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit et dit : « Lève-toi, descends à Qeïla, car je livre les Philistins dans ta main. »
fr.B: David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} une fois de plus, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit : « Mets-toi en route et descends à Qeïla, car je te livre les Philistins. »
fr.R: Alors David a encore posé la question {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a répondu : « Descends à Qeïla maintenant. Je vais te donner la victoire sur les Philistins. »

decisions.choice: inquired again: a second asking, because of the men's fear
decisions.reason: David asks the same question a second time after his men object (verse 3). The second answer repeats the first and adds a promise of victory, which answers their fear.

decisions.choice: giving into your hand: giving you power over them, victory
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The participle "giving" presents the victory as already under way.

decisions.choice: go down: from the hill country to the lower foothills
decisions.reason: Keilah lies in the foothills west of the hills of Judah, so David's men must go down to reach it, as Saul's men would (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Set out (Balanced); now (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Arise" here means to get moving, not to stand up. Balanced says "set out"; Readable gives the sense of urgency with "now".

decisions.choice: give you victory over
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "give into your hand".

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֩ וַאֲנָשָׁ֨יו קְעִילָ֜ה וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּנְהַג֙ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּ֥ךְ בָּהֶ֖ם מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣שַׁע דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֖ת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י קְעִילָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And went David and his men [to] Keilah, and fought against the Philistines, and drove off their livestock, and struck them [with] a great striking; and saved David [the] inhabitants of Keilah.

en.L: So David and his men went [to] Keilah and fought against the Philistines, and he drove off their livestock and struck them [with] a great blow. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
en.B: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He carried off their livestock and dealt them a heavy defeat. So David rescued the people of Keilah.
en.R: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. David took away their animals and killed a great many of them. That is how David saved the people of Keilah.

fr.L: Et David et ses hommes allèrent à Qeïla, et ils combattirent contre les Philistins, et il emmena leur bétail, et il les frappa d’un grand coup. Et David sauva les habitants de Qeïla.
fr.B: David et ses hommes allèrent donc à Qeïla et combattirent les Philistins. Il emmena leur bétail et leur infligea une lourde défaite. Ainsi David délivra les habitants de Qeïla.
fr.R: Alors David et ses hommes sont allés à Qeïla et ils ont combattu les Philistins. David a emmené leurs bêtes et il a tué un très grand nombre de Philistins. C’est ainsi que David a sauvé les habitants de Qeïla.

decisions.choice: his men: the written text uses an older spelling of the same word
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell "his men" in a short, older form; the scribes' marginal reading gives the usual form. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: drove off their livestock: took the Philistines' animals as plunder
decisions.reason: The text does not say why the Philistines had livestock with them; they may have brought animals for food or to carry off the stolen grain. Taking them turned the raiders' own goods into spoil.

decisions.choice: David saved Keilah: what the LORD promised is done
decisions.reason: The verse ends with the word the LORD used in verse 2, "save Keilah". The story shows the promise kept to the letter.

decisions.choice: killed a great many of them
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a "great blow" meant in battle.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּ֠בְרֹחַ אֶבְיָתָ֧ר בֶּן־אֲחִימֶ֛לֶךְ אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד קְעִילָ֑ה אֵפ֖וֹד יָרַ֥ד בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, in fleeing Abiathar son of Ahimelech to David [to] Keilah, an ephod came down in his hand.

en.L: And it was, when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David [at] Keilah, an ephod came down in his hand.
en.B: Now when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he came down with an ephod in his hand.
en.R: When Abiathar son of Ahimelech escaped and came to David at Keilah, he brought an ephod with him. The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Abiathar, fils d’Ahimélek, s’enfuit auprès de David à Qeïla, qu’un éphod descendit dans sa main.
fr.B: Or, quand Abiathar, fils d’Ahimélek, s’était enfui auprès de David à Qeïla, il était descendu avec un éphod à la main.
fr.R: Quand Abiathar, le fils d’Ahimélek, s’était échappé pour rejoindre David à Qeïla, il avait apporté un éphod avec lui. L’éphod était le vêtement du prêtre qui servait à demander des réponses à Dieu.

decisions.choice: a note looking back: how the ephod came to be with David
decisions.reason: The verse breaks off the story to explain something the reader needs for verse 9. Abiathar had escaped the killing of the priests at Nob and fled to David (22:20-23); here we learn that he joined him at Keilah and brought an ephod. The order of events is not given, so it is not clear whether David's earlier inquiries (verses 2 and 4) were made through Abiathar.

decisions.choice: ephod: the priestly garment used to seek an answer from God
decisions.reason: The ephod held the breastpiece with the Urim and Thummim, through which the LORD's will was asked (Exodus 28:6-30; see 14:3). This is probably the ephod kept at Nob, behind which Goliath's sword lay (21:10).

decisions.choice: fled to David at Keilah; an ephod came down in his hand
alternatives: he went down with David to Keilah with an ephod in his hand
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "he went down with David to Keilah, having an ephod in his hand", placing Abiathar's arrival before the battle. The Hebrew text is kept: Abiathar reached David at Keilah.

decisions.choice: came down in his hand: he carried it down with him
decisions.reason: The ephod is the grammatical subject, but the sense is that Abiathar brought it.

decisions.choice: he came down with an ephod in his hand (Balanced); he brought an ephod with him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Abiathar the subject, since an ephod cannot come down by itself.

decisions.choice: The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as at 14:3, because verses 9-12 depend on it.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְשָׁא֔וּל כִּי־בָ֥א דָוִ֖ד קְעִילָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל נִכַּ֨ר אֹת֤וֹ אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיָדִ֔י כִּ֚י נִסְגַּ֣ר לָב֔וֹא בְּעִ֖יר דְּלָתַ֥יִם וּבְרִֽיחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Saul that had come David [to] Keilah; and said Saul, Has made him a stranger God into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering into a city of doors and bar.

en.L: And it was told to Saul that David had come [to] Keilah. And Saul said, "God has given him up into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town of doors and bar."
en.B: Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, and he said, "God has handed him over to me. He has shut himself in by going into a town with gates and bars."
en.R: Someone told Saul that David had gone to Keilah. Saul said, "God has handed David over to me! He has trapped himself inside a town with gates that lock."

fr.L: Et on rapporta à Saül que David était venu à Qeïla. Et Saül dit : « Dieu l’a rejeté [et livré] dans ma main, car il s’est enfermé en entrant dans une ville à portes et à verrou. »
fr.B: On apprit à Saül que David était allé à Qeïla, et il dit : « Dieu me l’a livré. Il s’est lui-même enfermé en entrant dans une ville qui a des portes et des verrous. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un a dit à Saül que David était allé à Qeïla. Saül a dit : « Dieu m’a livré David ! Il s’est pris au piège dans une ville dont les portes ferment à clé. »

decisions.choice: has given him up: has disowned him and handed him over
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to treat someone as a stranger. With "into my hand" it means that God has cast David off and given him up to Saul.

decisions.choice: given up: the reading of the Hebrew text
alternatives: has sold him into my hand
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "has sold him", which in Hebrew differs by one letter. Both give the same sense, that God has delivered David to Saul; the Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: Saul claims God's help for his hunt
decisions.reason: Saul says God is with him against David, though the reader knows the LORD has left Saul and is with David (16:14; 18:12, 14). Verse 14 answers him: "God did not give him into his hand".

decisions.choice: a town of doors and bar: a walled town whose gates are barred
decisions.reason: The double doors of a town gate were closed with a heavy beam across them. A walled town gave protection, but it also became a trap if an army surrounded it.

decisions.choice: gates and bars (Balanced); gates that lock (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the town's gates and the bars that held them shut. Readable says what the bars did.

source.text: וַיְשַׁמַּ֥ע שָׁא֛וּל אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה לָרֶ֣דֶת קְעִילָ֔ה לָצ֥וּר אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד וְאֶל־אֲנָשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned Saul all the people for the war, to go down [to] Keilah to besiege David and his men.

en.L: And Saul summoned all the people for war, to go down [to] Keilah to besiege David and his men.
en.B: Saul called up all the troops for battle, to go down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.
en.R: So Saul called all his soldiers together for battle. He wanted to go down to Keilah and surround David and his men there.

fr.L: Et Saül convoqua tout le peuple pour la guerre, pour descendre à Qeïla assiéger David et ses hommes.
fr.B: Saül appela toutes ses troupes au combat, pour descendre à Qeïla et assiéger David et ses hommes.
fr.R: Alors Saül a rassemblé tous ses soldats pour la bataille. Il voulait descendre à Qeïla et encercler David et ses hommes dans la ville.

decisions.choice: all the people: the fighting men, the army
decisions.reason: Here "the people" are the men Saul calls out to fight, as in 11:11 and 15:4.

decisions.choice: besiege: surround the town and cut it off
decisions.reason: An army besieged a walled town by surrounding it so that no one could get in or out, until hunger forced it to give up. Saul means to trap David and his men inside.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); his soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" means the army here; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣דַע דָּוִ֔ד כִּ֣י עָלָ֔יו שָׁא֖וּל מַחֲרִ֣ישׁ הָרָעָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן הַגִּ֖ישָׁה הָאֵפֽוֹד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And knew David that against him Saul [was] devising the evil, and said to Abiathar the priest, Bring near the ephod.

en.L: And David knew that Saul was devising the evil against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod near."
en.B: When David learned that Saul was plotting harm against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."
en.R: David found out that Saul was planning to harm him. So he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."

fr.L: Et David sut que c’était contre lui que Saül tramait le mal, et il dit à Abiathar le prêtre : « Approche l’éphod. »
fr.B: Quand David apprit que Saül préparait un mauvais coup contre lui, il dit au prêtre Abiathar : « Apporte l’éphod. »
fr.R: David a appris que Saül voulait lui faire du mal. Alors il a dit au prêtre Abiathar : « Apporte l’éphod. »

decisions.choice: devising: planning, scheming
decisions.reason: The verb means to work out a plan, often a harmful one (Proverbs 3:29; 6:14). Saul's plan is the siege of verse 8.

decisions.choice: against him: put first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "against him" before Saul's name: David sees that the harm is aimed at him, and the town is in danger only because of him (verse 10).

decisions.choice: bring the ephod: so that the LORD can be asked
decisions.reason: David asks for the ephod in order to put his questions to the LORD through the priest, as he does again at Ziklag (30:7-8).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ דָּוִד֒ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שָׁמֹ֤עַ שָׁמַע֙ עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּֽי־מְבַקֵּ֥שׁ שָׁא֖וּל לָב֣וֹא אֶל־קְעִילָ֑ה לְשַׁחֵ֥ת לָעִ֖יר בַּעֲבוּרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Yahweh, God of Israel, hearing has heard your servant that [is] seeking Saul to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on account of me.

en.L: And David said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has surely heard that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on my account.
en.B: Then David said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has heard for certain that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me.
en.R: Then David prayed, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, have been told that Saul plans to come to Keilah. He wants to destroy the town because of me.

fr.L: Et David dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur a bien entendu dire que Saül cherche à venir à Qeïla pour détruire la ville à cause de moi.
fr.B: Puis David dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur a appris de façon certaine que Saül a l’intention de venir à Qeïla et de détruire la ville à cause de moi.
fr.R: Ensuite, David a prié : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, moi, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, j’ai appris que Saül veut venir à Qeïla. Il veut détruire la ville à cause de moi.

decisions.choice: has surely heard: the doubled verb stresses that the report is certain
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to strengthen it. David is not passing on a rumor; he has heard it plainly.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking to God or to a superior, a person called himself "your servant". David uses it throughout this prayer (verse 11).

decisions.choice: to destroy the city on my account: David fears for the town
decisions.reason: Saul had already wiped out the priests' town of Nob because of David (22:19). David fears that Keilah will suffer the same.

decisions.choice: David prayed; I, your servant, have been told
decisions.reason: Readable says that David is speaking to God, and joins "your servant" to "I" so that the reader sees David means himself.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} without the article when God is addressed; {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur
decisions.reason: French drops the article in direct address, as the published French Psalms do; the possessive for God takes the deity pronoun span, as the English "your".

source.text: הֲיַסְגִּרֻ֣נִי בַעֲלֵי֩ קְעִילָ֨ה בְיָד֜וֹ הֲיֵרֵ֣ד שָׁא֗וּל כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁמַ֣ע עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַגֶּד־נָ֖א לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָסוַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Will surrender me [the] lords of Keilah into his hand? Will come down Saul as has heard your servant? Yahweh, God of Israel, tell, please, to your servant. And said Yahweh, He will come down.

en.L: Will the lords of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has heard? {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, tell {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, please." And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "He will come down."
en.B: Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has heard? {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, please tell {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant." {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "He will come down."
en.R: Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to Saul? Will Saul really come down, as I have heard? {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, please tell me." {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "He will come down."

fr.L: Les seigneurs de Qeïla me livreront-ils dans sa main ? Saül descendra-t-il, comme {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur l’a entendu dire ? {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, fais-le savoir, je te prie, à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur. » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Il descendra. »
fr.B: Les notables de Qeïla me livreront-ils à lui ? Saül descendra-t-il, comme {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur l’a appris ? {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, fais-le savoir, je t’en prie, à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur. » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « Il descendra. »
fr.R: Est-ce que les notables de Qeïla vont me livrer à Saül ? Est-ce que Saül va vraiment descendre, comme je l’ai entendu dire ? {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, dis-le-moi, s’il te plaît. » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « Il descendra. »

decisions.choice: the lords of Keilah: the town's leading citizens
decisions.reason: The word means owners or masters. Used of a town it names the landholders who governed it and could decide its policy, as "the lords of Shechem" did (Judges 9:2-3).

decisions.choice: two questions, and the LORD answers the second first
decisions.reason: David asks whether the town will give him up and whether Saul will come. The LORD answers only the second, so in verse 12 David asks the first question again.

decisions.choice: surrender: shut in and hand over
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for shutting: the town that "shut" David in (verse 7) could also hand him over. Towns under siege bought peace by giving up the man the attacker wanted (2 Samuel 20:15-22).

decisions.choice: the leaders of Keilah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "leaders" for "lords", as at Judges 9:2, since the men are not nobles but the town's chief citizens.

decisions.choice: I; me
decisions.reason: Readable puts "your servant" in the first person, the plain sense of the polite form.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד הֲיַסְגִּ֜רוּ בַּעֲלֵ֧י קְעִילָ֛ה אֹתִ֥י וְאֶת־אֲנָשַׁ֖י בְּיַד־שָׁא֑וּל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יַסְגִּֽירוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Will surrender [the] lords of Keilah me and my men into [the] hand of Saul? And said Yahweh, They will surrender.

en.L: And David said, "Will the lords of Keilah surrender me and my men into [the] hand of Saul?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "They will surrender [you]."
en.B: David asked again, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "They will hand you over."
en.R: David asked again, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand my men and me over to Saul?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Yes, they will."

fr.L: Et David dit : « Les seigneurs de Qeïla me livreront-ils, moi et mes hommes, dans la main de Saül ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Ils [vous] livreront. »
fr.B: David demanda encore : « Les notables de Qeïla me livreront-ils à Saül, moi et mes hommes ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « Ils vous livreront. »
fr.R: David a demandé encore : « Est-ce que les notables de Qeïla vont nous livrer à Saül, mes hommes et moi ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « Oui. »

decisions.choice: they will surrender you: the LORD answers what would happen
decisions.reason: The answer tells what the men of Keilah would do if David stayed. David leaves (verse 13), so it does not happen. The LORD's answer lets David escape the danger rather than fixing his fate.

decisions.choice: they will surrender: the object is understood
decisions.reason: The LORD answers with the verb alone; "you" (David and his men) is understood from the question.

decisions.choice: asked again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "again", since David repeats his first question of verse 11.

decisions.choice: Yes, they will.
decisions.reason: Readable answers the yes-or-no question in the shortest natural way.

source.text: וַיָּקָם֩ דָּוִ֨ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ מִקְּעִלָ֔ה וַיִּֽתְהַלְּכ֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ וּלְשָׁא֣וּל הֻגַּ֗ד כִּֽי־נִמְלַ֤ט דָּוִד֙ מִקְּעִילָ֔ה וַיֶּחְדַּ֖ל לָצֵֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose David and his men, about six hundred man, and went out from Keilah and went about in [places] where they went about; and to Saul it was told that had escaped David from Keilah, and he ceased to go out.

en.L: And David and his men arose, about six hundred men, and went out from Keilah, and they went about wherever they went about. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, and he stopped going out.
en.B: So David and his men, about six hundred of them, set out and left Keilah, and they kept moving from place to place. Saul was told that David had slipped away from Keilah, and he called off the march.
en.R: So David and his men left Keilah. There were now about six hundred of them. They kept moving from one place to another. When Saul heard that David had escaped from Keilah, he did not go there after all.

fr.L: Et David se leva avec ses hommes, environ six cents hommes, et ils sortirent de Qeïla et allèrent là où ils allèrent. Et on rapporta à Saül que David s’était échappé de Qeïla, et il renonça à sortir.
fr.B: David et ses hommes, environ six cents, se mirent donc en route et quittèrent Qeïla, et ils allèrent d’un lieu à l’autre. Quand on apprit à Saül que David s’était échappé de Qeïla, il renonça à son expédition.
fr.R: Alors David et ses hommes ont quitté Qeïla. Maintenant, ils étaient environ six cents. Ils allaient sans cesse d’un endroit à un autre. Quand Saül a appris que David s’était échappé de Qeïla, il n’y est finalement pas allé.

decisions.choice: about six hundred men: David's band has grown
decisions.reason: About four hundred men had gathered to David at the cave of Adullam (22:2). Now there are about six hundred, the number he still has later (27:2; 30:9).

decisions.choice: went about wherever they went about: they kept on the move, with no fixed place
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in a phrase that leaves the destination open: they went wherever they could. It pictures men on the run, not settled anywhere.

decisions.choice: he stopped going out: Saul called off the campaign
decisions.reason: "Going out" is the word for an army marching out to war. Once David was no longer shut inside Keilah, Saul's plan of verse 8 had no point.

decisions.choice: There were now about six hundred of them.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the number a sentence of its own and adds "now" to show that the band had grown since 22:2.

decisions.choice: called off the march (Balanced); did not go there after all (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Saul's stopping meant: he gave up the march on Keilah.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב דָּוִ֤ד בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ בַּמְּצָד֔וֹת וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בָּהָ֖ר בְּמִדְבַּר־זִ֑יף וַיְבַקְשֵׁ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ כָּל־הַיָּמִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־נְתָנ֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And stayed David in the wilderness in the strongholds, and stayed in the hill country in [the] wilderness of Ziph; and sought him Saul all the days, and not gave him God into his hand.

en.L: And David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and he stayed in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him all the days, but God did not give him into his hand.
en.B: David stayed in the strongholds of the wilderness, in the hill country of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul searched for him day after day, but God did not give David into his hands.
en.R: David stayed out in the wilderness, in places that were hard to reach in the hills of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul looked for him every day, but God did not let Saul catch him.

fr.L: Et David demeura dans le désert, dans les forteresses, et il demeura dans la montagne, dans le désert de Ziph. Et Saül le chercha tous les jours, mais Dieu ne le livra pas dans sa main.
fr.B: David s’installa dans les forteresses du désert, dans la région montagneuse du désert de Ziph. Saül le cherchait jour après jour, mais Dieu ne le livra pas entre ses mains.
fr.R: David est resté dans le désert, dans des endroits difficiles d’accès, dans les collines du désert de Ziph. Saül le cherchait tous les jours, mais Dieu n’a pas laissé Saül l’attraper.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Ziph: dry hill country south of Hebron
decisions.reason: Ziph was a town in the hills of Judah a few miles south of Hebron (Joshua 15:55). East of it the land falls away in bare ridges and ravines toward the Dead Sea; it had pasture but few settlements, which made it a place to hide.

decisions.choice: strongholds: heights that are hard to reach
decisions.reason: The word names rugged places where people could hold out against attackers (Judges 6:2). David's camp is a natural fortress, not a built fort.

decisions.choice: God did not give him into his hand: the answer to Saul's claim
decisions.reason: In verse 7 Saul said, "God has given him up into my hand." The narrator now states the opposite, using the same picture of the hand: Saul searches without end, but God protects David.

decisions.choice: all the days: continually, day after day
decisions.reason: The phrase means the whole time, not one day only: Saul never stopped looking.

decisions.choice: places that were hard to reach; did not let Saul catch him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "strongholds" by what made them useful, as at Judges 6:2, and says plainly what "give into his hand" meant here.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא דָוִ֔דכִּֽי־יָצָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְדָוִ֥ד בְּמִדְבַּר־זִ֖יף בַּחֹֽרְשָׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And saw David that had come out Saul to seek his life; and David [was] in [the] wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.

en.L: And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life; and David [was] in the wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.
en.B: David saw that Saul had come out to take his life. At the time David was at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph.
en.R: David found out that Saul had come out to kill him. At that time David was at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph.

fr.L: Et David vit que Saül était sorti pour chercher sa vie ; et David [était] dans le désert de Ziph, à Horesh.
fr.B: David vit que Saül était sorti pour lui ôter la vie. David se trouvait alors à Horesh, dans le désert de Ziph.
fr.R: David a appris que Saül était sorti pour le tuer. À ce moment-là, David était à Horesh, dans le désert de Ziph.

decisions.choice: David saw: the vowels of the Hebrew text
alternatives: David was afraid because Saul had come out
decisions.reason: The same consonants can be read "David was afraid" with different vowels. The Hebrew text as pointed reads "saw", meaning he learned or realized; that reading is kept. "Was afraid" would fit Jonathan's words in verse 17, "Do not be afraid".

decisions.choice: seek his life: try to kill him
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" is to hunt him in order to kill him (20:1; 22:23).

decisions.choice: Horesh: a place name meaning "woodland" or "thicket"
decisions.reason: The word means a wooded or scrubby place, and could be read "in the woods". Here and in verses 16, 18 and 19 it names a particular spot in the wilderness of Ziph, so it is kept as a name.

decisions.choice: found out; to kill him
decisions.reason: Readable says "found out" for "saw" in the sense of learning, and "kill him" for "seek his life".

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד חֹ֑רְשָׁה וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק אֶת־יָד֖וֹ בֵּאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Jonathan son of Saul and went to David [to] Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.

en.L: And Jonathan son of Saul arose and went to David [at] Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.
en.B: Then Saul's son Jonathan set out and went to David at Horesh, and he gave him fresh strength in God.
en.R: Then Saul's son Jonathan went to see David at Horesh. He helped David find courage by trusting in God.

fr.L: Et Jonathan, fils de Saül, se leva et alla vers David à Horesh, et il fortifia sa main en Dieu.
fr.B: Alors Jonathan, le fils de Saül, se mit en route et alla trouver David à Horesh, et il lui redonna des forces en Dieu.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jonathan, le fils de Saül, est allé voir David à Horesh. Il l’a aidé à reprendre courage en faisant confiance à Dieu.

decisions.choice: strengthened his hand: gave him courage
decisions.reason: To strengthen someone's hands is to encourage him to act boldly (Judges 9:24; 2 Samuel 2:7; Nehemiah 2:18).

decisions.choice: in God: the strength comes from God
decisions.reason: Jonathan does not offer his own protection or his father's favor. He points David to God as the one who will keep him.

decisions.choice: son of Saul: the hunter's son comes to the hunted
decisions.reason: The narrator names Jonathan as Saul's son just when Saul is hunting David, to show how much Jonathan risks in coming.

decisions.choice: gave him fresh strength in God (Balanced); helped David find courage by trusting in God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom of the hand. Readable says how the strength was found in God: by trusting him.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו אַל־תִּירָ֗א כִּ֠י לֹ֤א תִֽמְצָאֲךָ֙ יַ֚ד שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֔י וְאַתָּה֙ תִּמְלֹ֣ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽהְיֶה־לְּךָ֣ לְמִשְׁנֶ֑ה וְגַם־שָׁא֥וּל אָבִ֖י יֹדֵ֥עַ כֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him, Not fear, for not will find you [the] hand of Saul my father; and you will reign over Israel, and I will be to you as second; and also Saul my father knows so.

en.L: And he said to him, "Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father will not find you. And you will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you. And even Saul my father knows this."
en.B: He said to him, "Do not be afraid. My father Saul will not lay his hand on you. You will reign over Israel, and I will be at your side as your second. Even my father Saul knows that this is so."
en.R: Jonathan told him, "Do not be afraid. My father Saul will not catch you. You will be king of Israel, and I will be second in command under you. Even my father Saul knows this."

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « N’aie pas peur, car la main de Saül, mon père, ne te trouvera pas. Et toi, tu régneras sur Israël, et moi, je serai le second après toi. Et même Saül, mon père, le sait bien. »
fr.B: Il lui dit : « N’aie pas peur. Mon père Saül ne mettra pas la main sur toi. Tu régneras sur Israël, et moi, je serai à tes côtés, le second après toi. Même mon père Saül sait qu’il en est ainsi. »
fr.R: Jonathan lui a dit : « N’aie pas peur. Mon père Saül ne t’attrapera pas. Tu seras roi d’Israël, et moi, je serai ton second, juste après toi. Même mon père Saül le sait. »

decisions.choice: the hand of Saul will not find you: Saul's power will not reach you
decisions.reason: When a hand "finds" someone it seizes him (Psalm 21:9). Jonathan promises that Saul will never lay hold of David.

decisions.choice: you will reign over Israel: Jonathan accepts David as the coming king
decisions.reason: Jonathan, the king's heir, says openly that the throne will go to David. He had already given David his robe and weapons (18:4) and asked for kindness to his family (20:13-16).

decisions.choice: second: second in rank, next to the king
decisions.reason: The word means the second in order or rank (2 Chronicles 28:7; Esther 10:3). Jonathan hopes to stand beside David as his chief helper. He died with Saul on Mount Gilboa (31:2), so this did not happen.

decisions.choice: Saul knows it: Saul himself is aware
decisions.reason: Saul had already told Jonathan that while David lived Jonathan's kingdom would not be secure (20:31), and later he says to David, "I know that you will surely be king" (24:21).

decisions.choice: second in command under you
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that "second" means rank.

source.text: וַיִּכְרְת֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם בְּרִ֖ית לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב דָּוִד֙ בַּחֹ֔רְשָׁה וִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן הָלַ֥ךְ לְבֵיתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And made [the] two of them a covenant before Yahweh; and stayed David at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.

en.L: And the two of them made a covenant before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And David stayed at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.
en.B: The two of them made a covenant in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then David stayed on at Horesh, while Jonathan went home.
en.R: The two of them made a covenant in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then Jonathan went back home, but David stayed at Horesh.

fr.L: Et tous deux conclurent une alliance devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et David demeura à Horesh, et Jonathan s’en alla chez lui.
fr.B: Tous deux conclurent une alliance devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Puis David resta à Horesh, tandis que Jonathan rentrait chez lui.
fr.R: Tous les deux ont fait une alliance devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ensuite, Jonathan est rentré chez lui, mais David est resté à Horesh.

decisions.choice: a covenant: the friends renew their bond
decisions.reason: Jonathan and David had made a covenant before (18:3; 20:8, 16-17, 42). Here they confirm it, now with Jonathan's hope of serving under David (verse 17).

decisions.choice: before the LORD: with the LORD as witness
decisions.reason: A covenant made "before the LORD" called on him to see it and hold both sides to it (20:23, 42). No altar or sanctuary is needed.

decisions.choice: Jonathan went home: their last meeting in the story
decisions.reason: This is the last time the two are seen together. Jonathan next appears at his death in battle (31:2).

decisions.choice: Then Jonathan went back home, but David stayed at Horesh.
decisions.reason: Readable puts Jonathan's leaving first, to make clear that they parted and David stayed behind.

source.text: וַיַּעֲל֤וּ זִפִים֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל הַגִּבְעָ֖תָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲל֣וֹא דָ֠וִד מִסְתַּתֵּ֨ר עִמָּ֤נוּ בַמְּצָדוֹת֙ בַּחֹ֔רְשָׁה בְּגִבְעַת֙ הַֽחֲכִילָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִימִ֥ין הַיְשִׁימֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Ziphites to Saul to the Gibeah, saying, [Is] not David hiding himself with us in the strongholds at Horesh, on [the] hill of the Hachilah, which [is] on [the] south of the Jeshimon?

en.L: And [the] Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is not David hiding himself among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which [is] to the south of the Jeshimon?
en.B: Some Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is David not hiding among us? He is in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, to the south of Jeshimon.
en.R: Some people from Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah. They said, "David is hiding in our area! He is in the hiding places at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, south of the Jeshimon wasteland.

fr.L: Et des Ziphiens montèrent auprès de Saül à Guibea, en disant : « David ne se cache-t-il pas chez nous dans les forteresses de Horesh, sur la colline de Hakila, qui [est] au sud du Yeshimôn ?
fr.B: Des Ziphiens montèrent trouver Saül à Guibea et lui dirent : « Ne sais-tu pas que David se cache chez nous ? Il est dans les forteresses de Horesh, sur la colline de Hakila, au sud du Yeshimôn.
fr.R: Des gens de Ziph sont allés voir Saül à Guibea. Ils lui ont dit : « David se cache dans notre région ! Il est dans les cachettes de Horesh, sur la colline de Hakila, au sud du désert du Yeshimôn.

decisions.choice: is not David hiding: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of announcing news: "You should know that David is hiding among us."

decisions.choice: Ziphites at Gibeah: men of Judah betray David to Saul
decisions.reason: The Ziphites belonged to David's own tribe of Judah, yet they go to Saul at his home and royal seat, Gibeah of Benjamin (10:26; 22:6), to give David up. They do so again at 26:1.

decisions.choice: the Ziphites: remembered in the title of Psalm 54
decisions.reason: The title of Psalm 54 (Psalm 54:2) refers to this event: "when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, Is not David hiding himself among us?"

decisions.choice: the Jeshimon: "the wasteland", the barren country toward the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The word means desolate land. With the article it names a region, the dry wilderness that falls away east of the hills of Judah (also verse 24; Numbers 21:20).

decisions.choice: David is hiding in our area!; the Jeshimon wasteland
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies, and adds "wasteland" to explain the name.

decisions.choice: les Ziphiens; Horesh, Hakila, le Yeshimôn
decisions.reason: The Ziphiens as the Samuel terms note sets; the other names, not in the table, in the usual French transcription, kept the same in chapter 26.

source.text: וְ֠עַתָּה לְכָל־אַוַּ֨ת נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לָרֶ֖דֶת רֵ֑ד וְלָ֥נוּ הַסְגִּיר֖וֹ בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, according to all [the] desire of your soul, O king, to come down, come down; and for us [is] to surrender him into [the] hand of the king.

en.L: And now, according to all the desire of your soul, O king, to come down, come down; and [it is] for us to surrender him into the hand of the king."
en.B: So now, O king, come down whenever you wish. Our part will be to hand him over to the king."
en.R: So, Your Majesty, come down whenever you want to. We will make sure that David is handed over to you."

fr.L: Et maintenant, selon tout le désir de ton âme, ô roi, de descendre, descends ; et [c’est] à nous de le livrer dans la main du roi. »
fr.B: Maintenant donc, ô roi, descends quand tu le désires. Notre affaire sera de le livrer entre les mains du roi. »
fr.R: Alors, ô roi, descends quand tu veux. Nous nous chargerons de te livrer David. »

decisions.choice: according to all the desire of your soul: as soon and as fully as you wish
decisions.reason: "Soul" here means the self and its longing. The phrase means "whenever you want" (Deuteronomy 12:15, 20).

decisions.choice: for us to surrender him: our task is to hand him over
decisions.reason: The Ziphites take the work on themselves: they will see that David is delivered. They use the verb David feared at Keilah (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: the king: a polite way of saying "you"
decisions.reason: Courtiers and subjects spoke of the king in the third person, as "the king", even to his face.

decisions.choice: O king
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the plain address "O king".

decisions.choice: Your Majesty; to you
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common form of address to a king and turns the polite "the king" into "you".

decisions.choice: ô roi
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "Your Majesty"; with "tu" to the king, as the Samuel terms note sets, French "ô roi" fits where "Majesté" would not.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל בְּרוּכִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י חֲמַלְתֶּ֖ם עָלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Saul, Blessed [are] you to Yahweh, for you have had compassion on me.

en.L: And Saul said, "Blessed [are] you by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for you have had compassion on me.
en.B: Saul said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, for you have shown me compassion.
en.R: Saul answered, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you for caring about me!

fr.L: Et Saül dit : « Soyez bénis {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car vous avez eu pitié de moi.
fr.B: Saül dit : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous bénisse, car vous avez eu pitié de moi.
fr.R: Saül a répondu : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous bénisse de vous soucier de moi !

decisions.choice: blessed are you by the LORD: a wish that the LORD will bless them
decisions.reason: This is a set form of blessing, both a greeting and a prayer for good from the LORD (15:13; Ruth 3:10; 2 Samuel 2:5).

decisions.choice: you have had compassion on me: Saul sees himself as the one wronged
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel pity and to spare. Saul speaks as if he were the victim; he had already complained that no one in his court felt sorry for him (22:8). Men who betray David are praised in the LORD's name.

decisions.choice: May the LORD bless you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the blessing as a wish, which is how it works.

source.text: לְכוּ־נָ֞א הָכִ֣ינוּ ע֗וֹד וּדְע֤וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־מְקוֹמוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה רַגְל֔וֹ מִ֥י רָאָ֖הוּ שָׁ֑ם כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עָר֥וֹם יַעְרִ֖ם הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Go, please, make sure yet, and know and see his place where is his foot, who has seen him there; for [one] has said to me, crafty he is very crafty.

en.L: Go, please, make [it] sure yet [more], and know and see his place where his foot is, [and] who has seen him there; for it has been said to me that he is very crafty.
en.B: Go now and make even more certain. Find out exactly where he goes and who has seen him there. I hear that he is very cunning.
en.R: Go and check again. Find out the exact place where he is staying, and who has seen him there. People tell me he is very clever and tricky.

fr.L: Allez donc, assurez-vous encore, et sachez et voyez l’endroit où est son pied, [et] qui l’a vu là ; car on m’a dit qu’il est très rusé.
fr.B: Allez, et assurez-vous-en encore mieux. Cherchez à savoir exactement où il va et qui l’a vu là. On m’a dit qu’il est très rusé.
fr.R: Allez vérifier encore. Trouvez l’endroit exact où il habite, et qui l’a vu là-bas. Les gens me disent qu’il est très malin et plein de ruses.

decisions.choice: where his foot is: the place where he moves about
decisions.reason: "His foot" stands for his steps: Saul wants to know the very spot where David goes and stays, not just the general area.

decisions.choice: who has seen him there: the Hebrew is abrupt
alternatives: see his place where he goes, quickly
decisions.reason: The words follow without a joining word, as if Saul were firing questions: where is he, and who has seen him? A small change in the letters would give "quickly" instead ("see where he is, quickly"), but the text as it stands makes sense and is kept.

decisions.choice: he is very crafty: the doubled verb stresses it
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to strengthen it. Saul has been told that David is shrewd and slippery, so his informers must be thorough.

decisions.choice: it has been said to me: the speaker is not named
decisions.reason: The verb "he said" has no stated subject and works as "someone told me".

decisions.choice: very clever and tricky
decisions.reason: Readable uses two plain words for the one Hebrew word, which means both shrewd and sly.

source.text: וּרְא֣וּ וּדְע֗וּ מִכֹּ֤ל הַמַּֽחֲבֹאִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְחַבֵּ֣א שָׁ֔ם וְשַׁבְתֶּ֤ם אֵלַי֙ אֶל־נָכ֔וֹן וְהָלַכְתִּ֖י אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְהָיָה֙ אִם־יֶשְׁנ֣וֹ בָאָ֔רֶץ וְחִפַּשְׂתִּ֣י אֹת֔וֹ בְּכֹ֖ל אַלְפֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And see and know from all the hiding places where he hides himself there, and return to me with certainty, and I will go with you; and it will be, if there is he in the land, and I will search him out among all [the] thousands of Judah.

en.L: And see and know all the hiding places where he hides himself, and return to me with certainty, and I will go with you. And it will be, if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah."
en.B: Look into every hiding place he uses and learn them all, then come back to me with sure information. Then I will go with you, and if he is anywhere in the region, I will hunt him down among all the clans of Judah."
en.R: Learn about all the places where he hides. Then come back and tell me what you know for sure. I will go with you, and if he is anywhere in the area, I will hunt him down. I will search through every clan in Judah!"

fr.L: Et voyez et sachez toutes les cachettes où il se cache, et revenez vers moi avec une certitude, et j’irai avec vous. Et il arrivera, s’il est dans le pays, que je le rechercherai parmi tous les milliers de Juda. »
fr.B: Observez toutes les cachettes qu’il utilise, et connaissez-les bien, puis revenez me voir avec des renseignements sûrs. Alors j’irai avec vous, et s’il se trouve dans la région, je le traquerai parmi tous les clans de Juda. »
fr.R: Découvrez tous les endroits où il se cache. Ensuite, revenez me dire ce que vous savez avec certitude. J’irai avec vous, et s’il est quelque part dans la région, je le trouverai. Je fouillerai tous les clans de Juda ! »

decisions.choice: the thousands of Judah: the clans of Judah
decisions.reason: "Thousand" can name a clan or a fighting unit drawn from one (10:19; Micah 5:1). Saul vows to search the whole tribe, clan by clan.

decisions.choice: with certainty: with sure, fixed information
decisions.reason: The word means something settled and firm. Saul wants a definite report before he sets out, after the failure at Keilah (verse 13).

decisions.choice: in the land: in the region
decisions.reason: "The land" here means the country round about, the territory of Judah, not the whole land of Israel.

decisions.choice: I will search him out: the verb means to search thoroughly
decisions.reason: The verb is used of searching every corner, as Laban searched Jacob's tent (Genesis 31:35).

decisions.choice: clans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "clans", because "thousands" would sound like a number of people rather than the groups of the tribe.

source.text: וַיָּק֛וּמוּ וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ זִ֖יפָה לִפְנֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְדָוִ֨ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו בְּמִדְבַּ֤ר מָעוֹן֙ בָּעֲרָבָ֔ה אֶ֖ל יְמִ֥ין הַיְשִׁימֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they arose and went to Ziph before Saul; and David and his men [were] in [the] wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah, to [the] south of the Jeshimon.

en.L: And they arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. And David and his men [were] in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah, to the south of the Jeshimon.
en.B: So they set out and went back to Ziph ahead of Saul. Meanwhile David and his men had gone on to the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.
en.R: So the men of Ziph went back home ahead of Saul. By now David and his men had moved to the wilderness of Maon. It was in the dry, open valley south of the Jeshimon wasteland.

fr.L: Et ils se levèrent et allèrent à Ziph devant Saül. Et David et ses hommes [étaient] dans le désert de Maôn, dans l’Araba, au sud du Yeshimôn.
fr.B: Ils partirent donc et retournèrent à Ziph avant Saül. Pendant ce temps, David et ses hommes étaient passés dans le désert de Maôn, dans l’Araba, au sud du Yeshimôn.
fr.R: Alors les gens de Ziph sont rentrés chez eux avant Saül. Pendant ce temps, David et ses hommes étaient allés dans le désert de Maôn. C’était dans la plaine sèche et dégagée, au sud du désert du Yeshimôn.

decisions.choice: Maon: a town in the hills of Judah, south of Ziph
decisions.reason: Maon is listed with Ziph and Carmel among the hill towns of Judah (Joshua 15:55), a few miles south of Ziph. Nabal later had his property there (25:2).

decisions.choice: the Arabah: dry, open lowland
decisions.reason: The word means desert plain or steppe. It often names the deep valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea; here it is the low, dry ground east of Maon that runs down toward the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: before Saul: ahead of him, with Saul to follow
decisions.reason: The Ziphites go home first to keep watch on David, and Saul is to come after them (verses 22-23).

decisions.choice: and David was in the wilderness of Maon: David had already moved
decisions.reason: The clause begins with David's name, not with a verb, which marks a situation in the background: while the Ziphites were away, David had gone farther south.

decisions.choice: the men of Ziph went back home; the dry, open valley
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are and explains "Arabah".

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ שָׁא֣וּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו֮ לְבַקֵּשׁ֒ וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְדָוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֣רֶד הַסֶּ֔לַע וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר מָע֑וֹן וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּרְדֹּ֥ף אַחֲרֵֽי־דָוִ֖ד מִדְבַּ֥ר מָעֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Saul and his men to seek, and told to David, and he went down the rock and stayed in [the] wilderness of Maon; and heard Saul and pursued after David [the] wilderness of Maon.

en.L: And Saul and his men went to seek [him], and they told David, and he went down [to] the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. And Saul heard, and he pursued after David [in the] wilderness of Maon.
en.B: Saul and his men went out to look for him. But David was told, so he went down to the rock and remained in the wilderness of Maon. Hearing of this, Saul went after David into the wilderness of Maon.
en.R: Saul and his men went out to search for David. But someone warned David, so he went down to the great rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. Saul heard where David had gone and chased him there.

fr.L: Et Saül et ses hommes allèrent [le] chercher, et on le rapporta à David, et il descendit [vers] le rocher, et il demeura dans le désert de Maôn. Et Saül l’apprit, et il poursuivit David [dans le] désert de Maôn.
fr.B: Saül et ses hommes partirent à sa recherche. Mais David fut averti ; il descendit vers le rocher et resta dans le désert de Maôn. Quand Saül l’apprit, il se lança à la poursuite de David dans le désert de Maôn.
fr.R: Saül et ses hommes sont partis chercher David. Mais quelqu’un a averti David. Alors il est descendu vers le grand rocher et il est resté dans le désert de Maôn. Saül a appris où David était allé, et il l’a poursuivi là-bas.

decisions.choice: the rock: a crag known to the first readers
decisions.reason: The article points to a particular rock, the one named at the end of the story (verse 28). It was probably a cliff or rocky ridge David could hide among.

decisions.choice: they told David: someone warned him
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the verb has no stated subject; the narrator does not say who brought David word.

decisions.choice: Saul heard: what he heard is understood
decisions.reason: Saul learned where David had gone and followed him.

decisions.choice: the great rock; heard where David had gone and chased him there
decisions.reason: Readable adds "great" to show that "the rock" is a landmark, says what Saul heard, and does not repeat the name of the wilderness.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ שָׁא֜וּל מִצַּ֤ד הָהָר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְדָוִ֧ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֛יו מִצַּ֥ד הָהָ֖ר מִזֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֨י דָוִ֜ד נֶחְפָּ֤ז לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וְשָׁא֣וּל וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו עֹֽטְרִ֛ים אֶל־דָּוִ֥ד וְאֶל־אֲנָשָׁ֖יו לְתָפְשָֽׂם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Saul from [the] side of the mountain from this, and David and his men from [the] side of the mountain from this; and was David hurrying to go from before Saul, and Saul and his men [were] surrounding to David and to his men to seize them.

en.L: And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain. And David was hurrying to get away from Saul, and Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men to seize them.
en.B: Saul moved along one side of the mountain while David and his men moved along the other. David was rushing to get clear of Saul, and Saul and his men were encircling David and his men to capture them.
en.R: Saul was going along one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other side. David hurried to get away from Saul. But Saul and his men were moving around the mountain to trap David and his men and take them.

fr.L: Et Saül allait de ce côté-ci de la montagne, et David et ses hommes de ce côté-là de la montagne. Et David se hâtait pour échapper à Saül, et Saül et ses hommes encerclaient David et ses hommes pour les saisir.
fr.B: Saül longeait un côté de la montagne, et David et ses hommes l’autre côté. David se hâtait pour échapper à Saül, et Saül et ses hommes encerclaient David et ses hommes pour s’emparer d’eux.
fr.R: Saül avançait d’un côté de la montagne, et David et ses hommes étaient de l’autre côté. David se dépêchait pour échapper à Saül. Mais Saül et ses hommes faisaient le tour de la montagne pour piéger David et ses hommes et les capturer.

decisions.choice: this side ... this side: one side and the other
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "from this ... from this" for two opposite sides. The mountain stands between the two groups.

decisions.choice: hurrying: hastening in alarm
decisions.reason: The verb means to hurry in fear, as when the nurse fled with Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 4:4).

decisions.choice: surrounding: closing in around
decisions.reason: The verb means to encircle. Saul's men are working around both sides of the mountain, so that David will be caught between them.

decisions.choice: was hurrying ... were surrounding: actions still under way
decisions.reason: The participles show the chase at its height, with nothing yet decided, which sets up the sudden turn in verse 27.

decisions.choice: moving around the mountain to trap David and his men and take them
decisions.reason: Readable says how the surrounding was done and what it was for.

source.text: וּמַלְאָ֣ךְ בָּ֔א אֶל־שָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹ֑ר מַהֲרָ֣ה וְלֵ֔כָה כִּֽי־פָשְׁט֥וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a messenger came to Saul, saying, Hurry and come, for have raided Philistines on the land.

en.L: And a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for [the] Philistines have made a raid on the land!"
en.B: But a messenger came to Saul and said, "Come quickly! The Philistines have raided the land."
en.R: Just then a messenger came to Saul. He said, "Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding our land!"

fr.L: Et un messager vint à Saül, en disant : « Hâte-toi et viens, car les Philistins ont fait une incursion dans le pays ! »
fr.B: Mais un messager vint dire à Saül : « Viens vite ! Les Philistins ont envahi le pays. »
fr.R: Juste à ce moment-là, un messager est arrivé auprès de Saül. Il lui a dit : « Viens vite ! Les Philistins attaquent notre pays ! »

decisions.choice: and a messenger came: a sudden turn
decisions.reason: The clause begins with "a messenger" rather than the verb, which breaks the flow of the chase: just as Saul is closing in, word arrives.

decisions.choice: made a raid: spread out to plunder
decisions.reason: The verb means to rush out and strip a place, used of raiding parties (27:8, 10; 30:1, 14).

decisions.choice: the Philistine raid saves David
decisions.reason: The narrator does not say that God sent the raid, but the story has already said that God did not give David into Saul's hand (verse 14). The Philistines, whom David had driven from Keilah, now draw Saul away from him.

decisions.choice: But (Balanced); Just then (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the sudden turn the Hebrew word order shows.

decisions.choice: our land
decisions.reason: Readable says whose land is meant: Saul's own country.

source.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב שָׁא֗וּל מִרְדֹף֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ לִקְרַ֣את פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים עַל־כֵּ֗ן קָֽרְאוּ֙ לַמָּק֣וֹם הַה֔וּא סֶ֖לַע הַֽמַּחְלְקֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned Saul from pursuing after David and went to meet Philistines; therefore they called the place the that Sela-hammahlekoth.

en.L: And Saul turned back from pursuing after David and went to meet [the] Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth.
en.B: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to face the Philistines. That is why that place was named Sela-hammahlekoth.
en.R: So Saul stopped chasing David and went to fight the Philistines. That is why people named that place Sela-hammahlekoth, which means "Rock of Parting."

fr.L: Et Saül cessa de poursuivre David, et il alla à la rencontre des Philistins. C’est pourquoi on appela ce lieu Séla-Hammahlekoth.
fr.B: Saül abandonna donc la poursuite de David et alla affronter les Philistins. C’est pourquoi on a appelé ce lieu Séla-Hammahlekoth.
fr.R: Alors Saül a arrêté de poursuivre David et il est allé combattre les Philistins. C’est pour cela que les gens ont appelé cet endroit Séla-Hammahlekoth, ce qui veut dire « Rocher de la séparation ».

decisions.choice: Sela-hammahlekoth: "the rock of parting"
decisions.reason: The name joins "rock" (the rock of verse 25) with a word from a root meaning to divide. It recalls how Saul and David were parted there, on two sides of the mountain, when Saul turned away. The same letters can also come from a root meaning smooth or slippery, giving "the rock of slipping away", the place where David escaped. The first sense is the more common use of the root, but both fit the story.

decisions.choice: therefore they called: the place took its name from this event
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject: people came to call the place by this name because of what happened there.

decisions.choice: went to meet the Philistines: went out to fight them
decisions.reason: "To meet" an enemy is to go out against him in battle (4:1; 17:48).

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text ends chapter 23 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 23 ends with this verse, and the next verse, about David going to En-gedi, is 24:1. Many Bibles number that verse 23:29, and so number the rest of chapter 24 one lower than here. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: Sela-hammahlekoth (Readable adds: which means "Rock of Parting")
decisions.reason: The name is kept at every level, as the name the place bore. Readable gives its likely meaning so that the reader can see how it sums up the story; the other possible sense is given in a footnote (m1).

decisions.choice: broke off his pursuit (Balanced); stopped chasing (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Turned back from pursuing" means that Saul gave up the chase.
